leadResults.answer: The gcc 15.2.0 register bookkeeping was run from the package text in the x86 model on a Stack laid out as the gcc code reads it: alloc_general_reg 0x36ae40, alloc_or_release_general_reg 0x36b020 and 0x39a300, alloc_avx_reg 0x36aa80 with Stack::alloc_avx_reg, both spill paths, Stack::pop and push, write_to_final_stack_offsets 0x3816e0 and block_prologue 0x392cd0. Over 12983 shift cases, 3000 block-exit cases, 4000 allocator cases and 4580 prologue cases (about 1.24 million sequence runs) no result differs from pyevm.py, no destination register or spill slot overwrites a live operand, the Stack bookkeeping stays consistent, and every one of 20 planted faults is caught. For the 22 non-literal shift sites the gcc stream equals the clang listing up to renaming. Stack states were generated, not logged from the clang harness, and whole blocks such as FullMath.mulDiv and Pool.swap were not driven end to end; the new lead names that step.

shift_general_reg_by_non_literal at 0x38e8c0, 0x38c8d0 and 0x389c90 and the inlined shift_avx_reg_by_non_literal in shl(), shr() and sar() give the specified word for counts 0, 1, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 191, 192, 255, 256, above 2^64 and random, and for negative values under SAR, in every operand location, with 0 mismatches. RoData's maps compare whole keys and never give two different words one label, including words built to share the hash. signextend_by_non_literal is not reached by any PoolManager code site. The two BYTE sites with a run-time index (src/libraries/BitMath.sol:22 and :45) read a literal value, which is the arm cycle 29 cleared; the only BYTE with two non-literal operands is in the metadata trailer and never runs. Neither arm was run.
